title: Preparing multi-arm trials for meta-analysis
text: Let’s make fake data three experiments. three continuous outcome. first small (N = 50) two arms. second larger (N = 100) three arms. third biggest (N = 200) four arms. use randomizr::complete_ra() assign treatment arm Z, performs complete random assignment automatically labels arms T1, T2, . Now estimate treatment effects estimatr::lm_robust(), returns heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors:
code: dat_1 <- data.frame(Z = complete_ra(50, num_arms = 2), Y = rnorm(50)) dat_2 <- data.frame(Z = complete_ra(100, num_arms = 3), Y = rnorm(100)) dat_3 <- data.frame(Z = complete_ra(200, num_arms = 4), Y = rnorm(200)) fit_1 <- lm_robust(Y ~ Z, data = dat_1) fit_2 <- lm_robust(Y ~ Z, data = dat_2) fit_3 <- lm_robust(Y ~ Z, data = dat_3)

title: Preparing multi-arm trials for meta-analysis
text: Meta-analyses multi-arm trials usually want standard errors clustered study, since arms study share variation block-diagonal vcov capture. Pass cluster column rma_mv_helper() wraps fit metafor::robust() , get cluster-robust standard errors one step: cluster = study evaluated estimates, exactly like yi. default clubSandwich = TRUE requests CR2 standard errors; set FALSE metafor’s CR0 estimator.
code: ev |>   rma_mv_helper(yi = estimate, random = ~ 1 | id, cluster = study) |>   tidy(conf.int = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 1 × 8 #>   term    type    estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high #>   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 overall summary    0.117    0.0961      1.22   0.374   -0.424     0.658

code: # Two experiments on overlapping subjects: every subject takes the survey # experiment, a random third also takes the lab experiment. The two effect # estimates are correlated, but there is no single regression to read the # covariance off, so bootstrap the design and use cov() of the replicates. set.seed(123) n <- 400 dat <- data.frame(   Z_survey = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),   in_lab = rbinom(n, 1, 1 / 3) ) dat$Z_lab <- ifelse(dat$in_lab == 1, rbinom(n, 1, 0.5), NA) dat$Y_survey <- 0.2 * dat$Z_survey + rnorm(n) dat$Y_lab <- 0.5 * dat$Z_lab + 0.6 * dat$Y_survey + rnorm(n)  estimate_both <- function(d) {   c(     survey = coef(lm(Y_survey ~ Z_survey, data = d))[["Z_survey"]],     lab = coef(lm(Y_lab ~ Z_lab, data = d[d$in_lab == 1, ]))[["Z_lab"]]   ) }  # Resample subjects, not rows within experiment, so the shared-sample # correlation is what the replicates reproduce boots <- t(replicate(200, estimate_both(dat[sample(n, n, replace = TRUE), ]))) V <- cov(boots) point <- estimate_both(dat)  estimates_df <- data.frame(   study = "study_1",   term = names(point),   estimate = point,   std.error = sqrt(diag(V)) )  ev <- make_estimates_vcov(estimates_df, V) ev #> <estimates_vcov> #> # 2 estimates with 2x2 vcov matrix #>  #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   id    study   term   estimate std.error #>   <chr> <chr>   <chr>     <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 1     study_1 survey    0.385     0.106 #> 2 2     study_1 lab       0.720     0.228 get_vcov(ev) #>             1           2 #> 1 0.011197075 0.003696527 #> 2 0.003696527 0.052076563

text: Breaking: estimates_vcov_from_pieces() renamed make_estimates_vcov(). deprecated alias kept, since package released. Previously described way recombine output get_estimates_df() get_vcov(), undersold . docs now state vcov matched estimates position dimnames matrix discarded, recommend supplying std.error rescale_estimates_vcov() standard errors rescale. vignette gains “Correlated estimates single regression” section working overlapping-samples bootstrap end end, bind_estimates_vcov() rma_mv_helper().
